Articles like this can be somewhat misleading, so I just thought I'd emphasize that this was done by a small group of SIX undergraduate students who all got elected to the student council because they got their friends to vote for them in student elections (I am assuming that nobody else on campus cares to participate in the student council or in student council elections for that matter just like at any other school I have ever been to).

From what I understand the student council is like a "play government," and this resolution was to ban showing the flag in a certain room that they had control over and NOT the campus at large. In other words, this was a bunch of kids getting their first taste of power and having no idea what to do with it. And so one of them (a major in social ecology? He might as well major in chronic unemployment) came up with an idea to do something offensive and stupid (as young kids tend to do), and it got passed because the morons in the student council outnumbered the sane people 6-4 (which shouldn't surprise anyone because joining the student council to begin with is a big fat waste of time).

Yet somehow this made national news and was taken to mean that their actions represent the beliefs of the school at large? Huh?!? How fair is that? This was obviously NOT an official action by the college, and it certainly doesn't represent the views of the average student at UC Irvine at all.
So a majority group of representatives, voted in by a popularity contest, passed a rule that nobody liked? Sounds like a lot of real governments from where I sit.
Clearly UC Irvine needs to reign in their student council before they get embarrassed by the national media again.
